# Module `lune_ui_core::paint`

[API reference](../INDEX.md) / parent [`lune_ui_core`](index.md)

Immediate-mode painter: every frame the UI is described from state into per-layer geometry,
text placements and hit regions. Clicks resolve against the previous frame's hit regions.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/paint.rs:1`

```rust
pub struct Painter<'a, H> {
```

Records one frame's drawing into a [`Scene`](scene.md#struct.Scene) and the hit regions of what it drew, at scale `s`.
Draw calls are in logical px; the painter turns them into physical px.

- <a id="method.Painter.acrylic"></a>`pub fn acrylic(&mut self, r: Rect, radius: f32, color: [f32; 4], under: [f32; 4], noise: bool)`

  The window's own background, on the fixed [`LayerId::Base`](scene.md#variant.LayerId.Base) layer: an acrylic layer with
  Skia `Src` semantics, which replaces what is below (`under` only feeds the antialiased
  edge). Colours premultiplied. The shape keeps `color` unfaded; the transform stack's alpha
  travels as the record's `opacity`, which the renderer blends the layer in with. Nothing is
  recorded when that opacity is not above zero.

  Anywhere else, on a fixed layer above `Base` or inside any overlay, it draws as
  [`Self::frost`](paint.md#method.Painter.frost) with the same colour and ignores `under`: no draw inside a window replaces
  what is below it, so none can open a hole to the desktop.

- <a id="method.Painter.acrylic_radii"></a>

  ```rust
      radii: [f32; 4],
      color: [f32; 4],
      under: [f32; 4],
      noise: bool,

  ```

  [`Self::acrylic`](paint.md#method.Painter.acrylic) with one radius per corner, in [`Self::fill_radii`](paint.md#method.Painter.fill_radii)'s order.

- <a id="method.Painter.arc"></a>`pub fn arc(&mut self, center: [f32; 2], radius: f32, start: f32, sweep: f32, style: StrokeStyle)`

  Strokes an arc of the circle of `radius` about `center` (logical px): from angle `start`
  over `sweep` radians, where 0 points right and a positive sweep turns clockwise on the
  screen. The polyline's chords stay within 0.25 device px of the circle. A `sweep` of 2π
  or more (either way) is a closed circle. A `radius` or `sweep` that is zero, or any value
  not finite, draws nothing.

- <a id="method.Painter.backdrop"></a>`pub fn backdrop(&mut self, r: Rect, radius: f32)`

  Ask for the blurred scene inside `r`, drawn under this layer, at the frame's sigma and
  saturation. See [`Self::backdrop_with`](paint.md#method.Painter.backdrop_with).

- <a id="method.Painter.backdrop_with"></a>`pub fn backdrop_with(&mut self, r: Rect, radius: f32, sigma: f32, saturation: f32)`

  [`Self::backdrop`](paint.md#method.Painter.backdrop) at its own `sigma` and `saturation` (0 means the frame's). Everything
  drawn before this layer is blurred, other glass included. Every request stands, and each has
  its own numbers; one that shows nothing (alpha 0, no area) records nothing.

- <a id="method.Painter.caret"></a>`pub fn caret(&mut self, spec: &Spec, offset: usize) -> CaretPos`

  Where the caret sits at byte `offset` of `spec`'s joined text ([`TextSystem::caret`](text.md#tymethod.TextSystem.caret)).

- <a id="method.Painter.clip_rect"></a>`pub fn clip_rect(&self) -> Option<Rect>`

  The current rect clip, in the space draws are made in now; `None` when no rect clips.

- <a id="method.Painter.custom"></a>`pub fn custom(&mut self, slot: usize, r: Rect)`

  Records an app-owned draw (the renderer's `CustomDraw` number `slot`) on the
  current layer, clipped to `r`, the current clip and the window. Nothing is recorded when
  that is empty. The clip is in physical px, left and top floored, right and bottom
  ceiled. The popup transform is ignored: custom items are not animated.

- <a id="method.Painter.dash"></a>`pub fn dash(&mut self, pts: &[[f32; 2]], closed: bool, width: f32, on: f32, off: f32, color: Rgba)`

  A dashed polyline: runs `on` long separated by gaps `off` long (logical px, along the path,
  starting with a run at the first point), each stroked `width` wide in `color`. `closed`
  also walks the segment from the last point back to the first. An `off` of 0 is a solid
  stroke; an `on` or `width` that is not above zero, or any value not finite, draws nothing.
  A pattern so fine that it would make over 100 000 runs is drawn solid.

- <a id="method.Painter.elide"></a>`pub fn elide(&mut self, spec: &Spec, max_w: f32) -> Spec`

  `spec` cut to `max_w` at this frame's scale: [`crate::text::elide`](text.md#fn.elide).

- <a id="method.Painter.fill"></a>`pub fn fill(&mut self, r: Rect, radius: f32, color: Rgba)`

  Fill below this layer's text.

- <a id="method.Painter.fill_joined"></a>`pub fn fill_joined(&mut self, parts: &[Vec<[f32; 2]>], outline: &[[f32; 2]], color: Rgba)`

  Fills one shape cut into `parts` (logical px) with `color`, below this layer's text: each
  part is a simple polygon, triangulated alone, so the cost stays linear in the parts however
  many there are; `outline` is the shape's one outer loop and alone gets the one-pixel
  antialiasing fringe, so no seam shows where two parts meet. The parts must tile the
  region `outline` bounds (a part outside it draws unfringed). A part the clipper cannot
  finish draws the triangles found, never panics; a part of over 4096 points draws nothing.
  Points that are not finite, in any part or the outline, draw nothing.

- <a id="method.Painter.fill_over"></a>`pub fn fill_over(&mut self, r: Rect, radius: f32, color: [f32; 4])`

  Fill above this layer's text (selection, cursor, overlays).

- <a id="method.Painter.fill_path"></a>`pub fn fill_path(&mut self, pts: &[[f32; 2]], color: Rgba)`

  Fills the simple polygon `pts` (logical px) with `color`, below this layer's text. Ear
  clipping triangulates it; a one-pixel fringe antialiases the edge. Holes and
  self-intersection are not supported: a polygon the clipper cannot finish (or one with over
  4096 points) draws the triangles found, never panics. Points that are not finite draw
  nothing.

- <a id="method.Painter.fill_radii"></a>`pub fn fill_radii(&mut self, r: Rect, radii: [f32; 4], color: Rgba)`

  [`Self::fill`](paint.md#method.Painter.fill) with a radius per corner: top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left.

- <a id="method.Painter.frost"></a>`pub fn frost(&mut self, r: Rect, radius: f32, color: [f32; 4], noise: bool)`

  The tint of a glass surface: premultiplied `color` over what is below, with the noise over
  it when `noise` is set. It draws with the shapes under the text, in record order; a
  [`Self::backdrop`](paint.md#method.Painter.backdrop) asked for first gives it something frosted to tint.

- <a id="method.Painter.frost_radii"></a>`pub fn frost_radii(&mut self, r: Rect, radii: [f32; 4], color: [f32; 4], noise: bool)`

- <a id="method.Painter.on"></a>`pub fn on(&mut self, layer: LayerId)`

  Draws on `layer` from now on. The clip stack and the transforms stay as they are: they belong
  to the code that pushed them, so a [`Self::pop_clip`](paint.md#method.Painter.pop_clip) after a layer change restores what its
  push replaced. (An overlay starts with none, [`Ui::overlay`](ui.md#method.Ui.overlay): it is
  not inside its opener's clip.) Items of one kind keep the order they were drawn
  in; the kinds draw in the renderer's order (acrylic, under shapes, path fills, customs,
  images, text, then over shapes and strokes, see [`crate::scene::Layer`](scene.md#struct.Layer)), so a fill drawn
  after a text still draws under it. The layers draw back to front ([`LayerId`](scene.md#enum.LayerId)). This is the
  fixed layer, whichever overlay is drawing: what an overlay draws after it is not the
  overlay's.

- <a id="method.Painter.pop_clip"></a>`pub fn pop_clip(&mut self)`

  Restores the clip that held before the last [`Self::push_clip`](paint.md#method.Painter.push_clip) or
  [`Self::push_clip_rounded`](paint.md#method.Painter.push_clip_rounded); does nothing without one.

- <a id="method.Painter.pop_translate"></a>`pub fn pop_translate(&mut self)`

  Removes the innermost transform, put there by [`Self::push_translate`](paint.md#method.Painter.push_translate), and moves the clips
  back; does nothing on an empty stack.

- <a id="method.Painter.pop_xform"></a>`pub fn pop_xform(&mut self)`

  Removes the innermost transform; does nothing on an empty stack.

- <a id="method.Painter.push_clip"></a>`pub fn push_clip(&mut self, rect: Rect)`

  Narrows the clip to `rect` intersected with the current clip, until the matching
  [`Self::pop_clip`](paint.md#method.Painter.pop_clip). The rect is in the space draws are made in now, like [`Self::set_clip`](paint.md#method.Painter.set_clip)'s.

- <a id="method.Painter.push_clip_rounded"></a>`pub fn push_clip_rounded(&mut self, rect: Rect, radius: f32)`

  [`Self::push_clip`](paint.md#method.Painter.push_clip) with the corners of `rect` rounded by `radius` (logical px, limited to
  half the shorter side): shapes, strokes, fills and images are cut along the rounded rect,
  antialiased; text and custom draws take its bounding rect only. The innermost rounded clip
  holds; a radius of 0 (or one that is negative or not finite) is a plain clip. A `rect` that
  is not finite clips everything.

- <a id="method.Painter.push_translate"></a>`pub fn push_translate(&mut self, dx: f32, dy: f32)`

  Adds a translation by `dx`, `dy` inside the current transforms, like
  [`Self::push_xform`](paint.md#method.Painter.push_xform) with [`Xform::translate`](paint.md#method.Xform.translate), and keeps the current clip and rounded clip
  where they are on screen (a plain `push_xform` moves them with the new space). Pair it with
  [`Self::pop_translate`](paint.md#method.Painter.pop_translate); a scroll area draws its content this way.

- <a id="method.Painter.push_xform"></a>`pub fn push_xform(&mut self, xform: Xform)`

  Adds `xform` inside the current ones: it applies first, the earlier ones after it.

- <a id="method.Painter.replay"></a>`pub fn replay(&mut self, ops: &Ops)`

  Replays `ops` through this painter's own methods, so the result depends on its current
  state (theme, scale, text system) as if the calls were made here.

- <a id="method.Painter.ring"></a>`pub fn ring(&mut self, r: Rect, radius: f32, width: f32, color: Rgba, above_text: bool)`

  1px-style outline inside `r`.

- <a id="method.Painter.sector"></a>`pub fn sector(&mut self, center: [f32; 2], radius: f32, start: f32, sweep: f32, color: Rgba)`

  Fills the circular sector of `radius` about `center` (logical px) from angle `start` over
  `sweep`, with the angle convention of [`Self::arc`](paint.md#method.Painter.arc), as one fan below this layer's text:
  one pass, so no seam shows at the centre. A `sweep` of 2π or more is the whole disc. A
  `radius` or `sweep` that is zero, or any value not finite, draws nothing.

<a id="struct.StrokeStyle"></a>
### Struct `StrokeStyle`

```rust
pub struct StrokeStyle {
    pub color: [f32; 4],
    pub width: f32,
    pub mode: f32,
    pub a: f32,
    pub b: f32,
    pub extra: [f32; 4],
}
```

How a stroke is drawn. Every length is in logical px of the drawing space, like the points;
the painter turns them into the units the shader reads.

`mode` 0 is solid. Mode 1, the conic sweep: `a` is the phase in turns, `extra[0..2]` the centre.
Mode 2, the comet: `a` the dash length, `b` the distance travelled, `extra[2]` the contour.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/paint.rs:86`
